name: TPS22993RLWR
title: TPS22993: four-channel 15 mΩ load switch, 1.0 V to 3.6 V, with GPIO and I2C control
summary: Four independent N-channel MOSFET load switches for rails between 1.0 V and 3.6 V, each carrying up to 1.2 A continuously with about 15 mΩ on-resistance when the separate VBIAS supply (4.5 V to 17.2 V) is at 7.2 V. After VBIAS comes up every channel follows its own active-high ON pin; over I2C (up to 1 MHz, seven addresses set by three pins) any channel can be handed to register control, and each channel's turn-on slew (five settings), turn-on delay (four) and output discharge resistance (four) can be chosen. A shared SwitchALL address lets one command load a stored on/off pattern into every device on the bus at once. It comes in a 3 mm × 3 mm 20-terminal WQFN (RLW) rated for -40 °C to 85 °C.
key_figures: 15 mΩ typ, 20 mΩ max at 25 °C (VBIAS = 7.2 V, IOUT = -200 mA)

circuits.title: Simplified schematic
circuits.description: Four rails from a PMIC each pass through one channel to a load drawn as a capacitor and resistor. Each input has its own capacitor to ground, the ON pins are the GPIO controls, VBIAS and VDD come from their own supplies, and a microcontroller talks to the part on SDA and SCL. The address pins are brought out for strapping to VDD or GND.

circuits.title: Cold-boot enable
circuits.description: Every ON pin is wired to its own channel's input, so each channel turns on as soon as its input rail appears, before the I2C bus is running. Once the bus is up, a channel can be moved to I2C control and switched off.

circuits.title: Power sequencing without I2C
circuits.description: Channel 3 is enabled by its own input; its output drives ON1, channel 1's output drives ON2 and channel 2's output drives ON4, so the outputs come up in the order VOUT3, VOUT1, VOUT2, VOUT4 with the default slew, delay and discharge settings and no bus traffic.

circuits.title: Four channels in parallel
circuits.description: All four inputs share one rail and all four outputs one load, with the four ON pins joined to a single GPIO, so the channels switch together as one switch with a quarter of the on-resistance and four times the current rating.

circuits.title: Switching-time test circuit
circuits.description: One channel between a voltage source with a 1 µF input capacitor and a load of CL in parallel with RL, switched by a step on its ON pin. tON and tOFF run from 50 % of VONx to 50 % of VOUTx, tD from 50 % of VONx to 10 % of VOUTx, and tR and tF between 10 % and 90 % of VOUTx.
notes: The switching characteristics use RL = 10 Ω and CL = 0.1 µF.

operation.text: VBIAS (4.5 V to 17.2 V) powers the device; it suits two- to four-cell Li-ion packs. Each VINx carries 1.0 V to 3.6 V, and VDD (1.62 V to 3.6 V) supplies only the I2C interface and must be the rail the SDA and SCL pull-ups return to.

When VBIAS is applied every register takes its default and all four channels follow their ON pins. ON is active high with a 1.05 V minimum high threshold, so a GPIO from 1.2 V logic upward drives it; ON pins must not be left floating. Rise time is controlled internally to limit inrush.

operation.topic: Moving between GPIO and I2C control
operation.text: Bits 7 to 4 of the control register (05h) choose, per channel, the ON pin (0) or I2C (1); bits 3 to 0 then turn an I2C channel off or on. The change can be made at any time while the bus is valid. To hand a channel over without a glitch, first write the control bit that moves it to I2C, then a second write that enables it.

Registers 01h to 04h hold, for channels 1 to 4, the ON delay (bits 6:5), the slew rate (bits 4:2) and the output-discharge resistance (bits 1:0). Slew settings 101 and 110 are invalid and 111 is reserved. The defaults are 11 µs delay, 460 µs/V slew and 951 Ω discharge.

Twelve mode registers (06h to 11h) each store an on/off pattern in their low four bits. A SwitchALL command, sent to address EEh followed by a mode-register address, copies that register's bits 3 to 0 into bits 3 to 0 of the control register in every TPS22993 on the bus at once, so as many as twelve stored power states can be applied with one 20-clock command.

The interface works at standard (100 kHz), fast (400 kHz) and fast-mode plus (1 MHz) speeds and may share a bus with 3.4 MHz devices, though it does not answer above 1 MHz. SDA and SCL are open drain and need pull-ups to VDD sized from the pull-up curves for the bus capacitance and VDD. Three address pins, each tied to VDD or GND, give seven addresses; with I2C unused, tie them to GND. The address inputs are high impedance, so pull-up resistors on them are optional.

A write sends the slave address with R/W = 0, a sub-address byte whose top bit enables auto-increment and whose low bits hold the register address, and then data bytes. A read first writes the sub-address, then repeats START with the address and R/W = 1; without the preceding write the register pointer is undefined. With auto-increment set the pointer advances after each byte, so consecutive registers are read or written in one transfer; non-consecutive registers need separate commands. Every byte is eight bits.
The 17 registers (four configuration, one control, twelve mode) return to their defaults whenever VBIAS is cycled, so non-default settings must be written again after each power-up.

A 1 µF ceramic capacitor from each VIN to GND close to the pins usually holds the input up when a channel switches into an empty load capacitor; more can be used for heavy loads. CIN should be about ten times CL, and at least a hundred times CL at the fastest slew setting. Because the NMOS body diode conducts from VOUT to VIN, a CL larger than CIN can drive VOUT above VIN and current back into the input when the supply is removed.
When a channel is off its output can be pulled to GND through 110 Ω, 490 Ω or 951 Ω, or left at high impedance, chosen per channel by QOD.
Channels may be joined for lower resistance or more current. Their ON pins are joined for synchronous GPIO control; under I2C one control-register write switches them together.

Keep traces short and the input and output capacitors next to the device to limit trace inductance. Wide VIN, VOUT and GND traces reduce parasitics and help heat flow from the package to the air. Keep the junction at or below 125 °C in normal operation.
